brand.name: shizue
brand.tagline: Your own plot, from a little spark of imagination.

common.confirmDelete: Delete this? This can't be undone.

plots.title: My plots
plots.subtitle: Import a card or start a plot from scratch.
plots.importHint: png · json · charx · jpg(charx) card file — the card arrives as the first character of a new plot.
plots.name: Name
plots.emptyHint: Import a card or create a new plot to get started.
plots.confirmDelete: Delete this plot? Its characters, assets and chats go with it.
plots.draftHint: One premise becomes a first version. The draft opens in the editor, yours to rewrite.
plots.draftPremisePlaceholder: e.g. On a rainy night, a stranger knocks at a bookshop that has already closed.
plots.draftGuideInput: Only your premise (up to 2,000 characters) and a fixed set of writing rules — none of your other plots or chats. In the premise’s language, the model writes a title, a one-line intro, the setting, 1–3 characters, 1–2 openings and tags.
plots.draftGuideModel: The model preset picked above writes it. At first that is the default sub model (or the default model), and this browser remembers your last pick. It is called with that preset’s key or ChatGPT plan.
plots.draftGuideResult: A draft is a suggestion. It becomes a new plot that opens in the editor. Rewrite it or delete it. If no draft comes back, nothing is created.
plots.draftGuideChoice: Lighter models are faster and spare your usage; larger ones are slower but follow the premise more faithfully. ChatGPT plans count usage per model. A draft stops after a minute.
plots.stImportHint: Bring over SillyTavern characters, groups, personas and chats all at once.
plots.pasteImportHint: Bring over a character you made on another platform, such as Zeta or Elyn, by pasting it in field by field.

plot.name: Title
plot.introHint: Shown on the work's card and the plot page. It is never sent to the model.
plot.introPlaceholder: e.g. A city divided between five guilds. You arrived belonging to none of them.
plot.coverHint: Used on the work's card and the plot page. A portrait 2:3 image fits without cropping. png · jpg · gif · webp · up to 5MB
plot.tagsHint: Enter or comma to add · up to 10
plot.languageHint: The language this plot was written in. When it isn't your language, a chat's language mode goes by it for the reply language and translation.
plot.descriptionHint: Goes in at the front of the prompt as the plot block. Write the setting, era and rules every character shares.
plot.descriptionPlaceholder: e.g. A city-state where magic is common, divided between five guilds.
plot.narratorVoiceHint: How the scene is described. Applies to narration, not to a character's own lines.
plot.narratorPovHint: Whose eyes the scene is told through. Pick third person limited to keep the user character's inner thoughts from being written for them.
plot.narratorPovThirdLimited: Third person limited — the scene and the characters only, never the user's inner thoughts
plot.styleHint: How the work is written. Only the options you set become directives in the prompt.
plot.membersHint: Every character and the narrator appear in the same chat. The order is the order they are introduced to the model in.
plot.memberImportHint: Adds a png · json · charx · jpg(charx) card file as a character.
plot.memberIntroHint: Shown in the cast list on the plot page. It is never sent to the model.
plot.memberIntroPlaceholder: e.g. The childhood friend who came back after five years. You still don't know why he left.
plot.memberDescriptionHint: Tells the model who this character is.
plot.memberMesExampleHint: Voice traits and lines across different situations. Separate the blocks with '<START>'.
plot.memberSystemPromptHint: Only the first character's is used, in place of the default writing instructions for the whole plot. Write '{{original}}' where the default should go; leave it empty to keep the default.
plot.memberPostHistoryHint: Added after the conversation on every turn, where the model follows instructions most closely. Only the first character's is used, in place of the default there. Write '{{original}}' where the default should go.
plot.memberUtilityBotHint: A RisuAI card setting. On, the card is sent as RisuAI sends a bot made for utility rather than roleplay: replies asked of it get none of the default instructions, the reply format hint, the persona or the author’s note — only the card’s description, lorebook, the conversation and its closing instructions. The card’s system prompt is not used either.
plot.memberFirstOnlyIdle: Only the first character ({first}) is read for this field, so this one is not used. Move this character to the top to use it.
plot.memberLorebookHint: This character's own lorebook. It is merged after the plot lorebook into one book that shares the same token budget.
plot.memberExportHint: Exports the saved card with the plot's openings, lorebook, narrator and custom UI. SillyTavern and RisuAI can read it. To take the plot's images along too, pick CharX.
plot.groupFlowHint: With two or more characters, a round of replies answers you one character at a time, each in its own bubble.

groupOrderHints.natural: Characters named in the text speak first, and the rest join by their talkativeness. Whoever just spoke sits the next round out.
groupOrderHints.list: Every character whose talkativeness is above 0 speaks, in roster order.

plot.groupCost: Each speaker is a separate generation, so more speakers per round mean more model usage.
plot.talkativenessHint: How readily the character joins a round on its own. At 0 it speaks only when the reader picks it.
plot.avatarHint: png · jpg · gif · webp · up to 5MB
plot.introsHint: The first scene a reader picks to start from. Up to 10 of them, and a chat swipes between them.
plot.introsEmpty: No openings yet. Without one, a chat starts with the reader's first message.
plot.introTextPlaceholder:
e.g. The rain had not stopped all night.
Sera: *She folds the umbrella and pushes the door open.* "You're late. I waited."
plot.speechProtocolHint: A 'Name: line' is that character speaking; a line with no prefix describes the scene. In a work with one character, that description is drawn inside the character's bubble too. Wrap action and expression in *asterisks* inside the line.
plot.sceneTitleHint: A '# Title' line shows as a large scene heading, and goes to the model as written.
plot.lorebookHint: Merged with the characters' own lorebooks and activated within the same token budget.
plot.loreBudgetUsage: Always-included entries ≈ {constant, number} tokens / budget {budget, number} tokens
plot.loreBudgetUsageAuto: Always-included entries ≈ {constant, number} tokens / budget automatic — {share, number, percent} of the chat context (about {budget, number} tokens by default)
plot.loreBudgetHint: Always-included tokens are counted from the saved plot lorebook and every saved card lorebook.
plot.loreBudgetInputHint: Saved on the first character's card ({first}) and applied to the whole book. Leave it empty for automatic.
plot.loreBudgetOver: The always-included entries alone exceed the budget. The budget fills from the highest insertion order down, so lower-ordered entries, always-included or matched by a keyword, are dropped and never reach the model. Raise the budget, or move what every turn needs into a character's description.
plot.lorebookImportHint: Adds the entries of a SillyTavern World Info file or a character card JSON after this lorebook's. Save to keep them.
plot.lorebookImported: Added {count, plural, one {# entry} other {# entries}}. Save to keep them.
plot.lorebookImportFailed: Couldn't read a lorebook. Check that it is a SillyTavern World Info or character card JSON file.
plot.loreNameHint: A label for finding the entry in the studio. It is never sent to the AI.
plot.loreAdvancedHint: Leave a field empty for the default. Scan depth, delay, sticky and cooldown count messages.
plot.loreGroupHint: Of the entries in one group that trigger together, only one is inserted, picked by weight. Separate several groups with commas.
plot.loreDepthHint: Leave empty to place it by its position. 0 goes after the last message, N before the Nth message from the end.
plot.loreOutletNameHint: Goes only where text that reaches the prompt, like a description or another entry, says '{{outlet::name}}'. Named nowhere, it is not sent.
plot.assetsHint: Write '{{img::slug}}' in an opening or a message to show the image.
plot.assetFonts: {count, plural, one {# web font file} other {# web font files}} the card used came along with the import. The stylesheet points at them.
plot.customUiHint: Turns patterns in the model's output into on-screen elements such as status panels and gauges. The stored conversation is untouched.
plot.displayScriptsHint: A regular expression selects part of a message and an HTML template draws it. Scripts run in order, each also matching what the earlier ones drew. Importing a RisuAI card brings its editdisplay scripts here.
plot.creatorCssHint: CSS for the markup your display scripts draw. It applies inside messages only, and only allowed properties are kept. Importing a RisuAI card brings the '<style>' from its background HTML here.
plot.displayScriptOutHint: Bind captures with $1-$99, and use the '{{getvar::key}} {{calc::expr}} {{#if expr}} {{#each list}} {{img::slug}} {{button::label::text}}' macros.
plot.displayScriptMemberHint: Pick a character and the script is not drawn on messages another character speaks. Messages no character speaks (openings, the reader’s turns) count as the first character’s.
plot.displayScriptRangeHint: 0 = the newest message, 1 = the one before it. Leave empty for every message. Messages hidden from the AI are not counted.
plot.memberCssHint: Applies only to messages this character speaks. Messages no character speaks (openings, the reader’s turns) count as the first character’s. Importing a RisuAI card as a character brings the '<style>' from its background HTML here.
plot.workBackgroundHint: HTML drawn behind the conversation. A work has one however many characters it has, and no character card’s background is drawn. Making a work from a RisuAI card brings that card’s background HTML (without its '<style>') here. Leave it empty to draw no background.
plot.modulesHint: A module’s lorebook, regex scripts, triggers (Lua included), pictures and background become the whole work’s, and run for every character after the card’s own, as in RisuAI. Changes here apply right away, without Save.
plot.moduleImportHint: Pick a RisuAI module (.charx, .risum or module JSON), a lorebook (RisuAI or SillyTavern JSON) or a RisuAI regex export. Each file becomes one module.
plot.moduleRemoveConfirm: Remove the module “{name}” from this work? The pictures it brought are deleted too.
plot.memberImportVariableConflicts: The work already had other values for {name}’s default variables {names}, so it kept them. Characters share their variables.
plot.defaultVariablesHint: Starting values for the chat variables. During a chat they change through the '{{setvar::key::value}} {{addvar::key::delta}}' macros.
plot.componentCodeSectionHint: Draws the call codes in a message ('<StatusWindow hp={50} />') as JSX components. The code runs only inside a sandboxed iframe, with no access to the app, the API or your cookies.
plot.componentCodeHint: A React subset: hooks limited to useState/useEffect/useMemo/useCallback/useRef, inline object styles only (no className, no string style), no timers, no network, no imports. Props come from the call code; platform state arrives as the platform prop ('{variables, turn, char, user, assets, suggestInput}').
plot.componentNone: No components yet. Declare a function whose name starts with a capital letter and a call code can name it.
plot.componentCallHint: The call code the model will write into a reply. Values must be JSON literals.
plot.componentCallUnrecognized: No declared component matches this call code.

patternError.too_long: This pattern is too long. Keep it under 10,000 characters.
patternError.invalid: This is not a valid regular expression.
patternError.unsafe_repetition: Inside a repeated group (* + '{n,}'), a repeat must be closed at once by a character it cannot match, as in (⟦[^⟧]*⟧)+, and a | choice must be plain words none of which starts another, as in (cat|dog)+. Shapes like (a+)+ or (a|aa)+ can freeze the browser.

plot.componentSendTurnHint: With this on, a component may take a turn for the reader through platform.sendTurn(text, '{ directions }'). The reader still grants it once per chat, and only one such turn is allowed per model turn.
plot.profilesHint: Who this plot is written to be read as. Picking one copies it into the reader’s own personas, where they can edit it freely.
plot.profileDescriptionPlaceholder: Say who the reader is while reading as this profile.
plot.profilePicked: A recommended profile is used instead of a persona.
plot.noModels: Make a model preset in Settings › Models first.
plot.chatsEmpty: No chats with this plot yet.
plot.memberEmotionHint: How the card's {count} expression images are shown. The panel beside the chat (above it on a narrow screen) shows the expression the auxiliary model picks after each reply; in the message, the model names one at the end of its reply and it is drawn there.
plot.chatImportHint: Brings a RisuAI chat file (.json, .html) or a SillyTavern chat (.jsonl) in as a chat of this work.
plot.chatImportAlready: {count, plural, one {# was already imported and was skipped.} other {# were already imported and were skipped.}}
plot.chatImportFailed: {count, plural, one {# could not be imported: {reason}} other {# could not be imported: {reason}}}
plot.chatImportNoData: This file has no chat to import.
plot.chatImportBookmarks: {count, plural, one {# bookmark was not brought over — shizue has no bookmarks.} other {# bookmarks were not brought over — shizue has no bookmarks.}}
plot.chatImportUnknownSpeaker: {count, plural, one {# reply whose member could not be told came in as the scene’s text.} other {# replies whose member could not be told came in as the scene’s text.}}
plot.chatImportSwipes: {count, plural, one {# alternative version past the limit was left out.} other {# alternative versions past the limit were left out.}}

cardImport.realmHint: Your browser downloads the card straight from RisuRealm. Cards up to 1GB can be imported.
cardImport.importWarnings: Not everything on the card came along:

importWarning.assets_unsupported: {count, plural, one {# file} other {# files}} that are neither a picture nor music
importWarning.assets_missing: {count, plural, one {# file} other {# files}} the card names but does not contain
importWarning.assets_over_budget: {count, plural, one {# file} other {# files}} past the import size limit
importWarning.assets_over_limit: {count, plural, one {# file} other {# files}} past the work’s limit of 10,000
importWarning.greetings_over_limit: {count, plural, one {# greeting} other {# greetings}} past the limit of 10 openings
importWarning.greetings_cut: {count, plural, one {# greeting} other {# greetings}} cut to 400,000 characters
importWarning.external_failed: {count, plural, one {# picture, font or stylesheet} other {# pictures, fonts or stylesheets}} on other sites that could not be brought in (the chat won’t show them)
importWarning.external_over_limit: {count, plural, one {# picture, font or stylesheet} other {# pictures, fonts or stylesheets}} on other sites left past the import’s limits
importWarning.module_mcp_inert: {count, plural, one {# module MCP server} other {# module MCP servers}}, never connected to
importWarning.module_cjs_inert: {count, plural, one {# piece} other {# pieces}} of module cjs code, never run

progress.localizing: Fetching images and fonts from other sites…

stImport.title: Move from SillyTavern
stImport.subtitle: Bring over the characters, groups, personas and chats you had in SillyTavern, all at once.

choose.zipHint: Choose the zip you saved from SillyTavern's User Settings → Account → Download Backup.
choose.folderHint: Choose the data/default-user folder inside your SillyTavern install.
choose.privacy: The backup is read inside this browser. Only the character cards you pick, their lorebooks and the converted chats are uploaded — settings.json, secrets.json, backgrounds, thumbnails, vectors and every other file stay on your device.

scan.checking: Comparing with what's already in shizue…

review.summary: Found {characters, plural, one {# character} other {# characters}}, {groups, plural, one {# group} other {# groups}}, {personas, plural, one {# persona} other {# personas}} and {chats, plural, one {# chat} other {# chats}}.
review.charactersHint: Each character becomes a plot of its own with them as its first character, and their chats come along.
review.groupsHint: Each group becomes one plot with every member in the cast, and the group chats come along.
review.chatsIncomplete: {count, plural, one {# interrupted chat starts} other {# interrupted chats start}} over
review.worldMissing: The linked lorebook file ({name}) is missing, so the card's own lorebook is used.
review.unspeakable: This name is over 40 characters or contains a colon, so chats can't recognize it as a speaker. Imported lines may read as narration.
review.extraWorlds: {count, plural, one {# extra lorebook} other {# extra lorebooks}}
review.noMembers: None of the members has a card here, so the group can't be imported.
review.overflow: A plot holds up to 10 characters, so these members are left out: {names}
review.missing: Left out for lack of a card: {names}
review.strategyManual: SillyTavern's Manual order has no match here, so the group comes in on natural order with one character answering each round. You can pick who speaks with Next turn in the chat.
review.strategyPooled: SillyTavern's Pooled order has no match here, so the group comes in on natural order with one character answering each round.
review.disabledMembers: Members muted in SillyTavern come in with talkativeness 0 (only when picked): {names}
review.personaExists: A persona with this name already exists.
review.memoryNotice: Summarizing long imported chats uses your ChatGPT plan's usage.
review.optionGlobalLorebooks: Attach the global lorebooks ({names}) to every imported plot
review.optionGlobalRegex: Add the {count, plural, one {# global regex script} other {# global regex scripts}} as display scripts
review.notImportedList: Presets, Instruct and Context templates, Quick Replies, themes, backgrounds, the Data Bank, vectors and extensions are not brought over.
review.skippedFiles: {count, plural, one {# file not read} other {# files not read}}
review.start: Import {count, plural, one {# item} other {# items}}

run.cancelledNotice: Retrying picks up the stopped items. A chat that was mid-import starts over.

reasons.persona_exists: A persona with this name already exists.
reasons.owner_failed: Skipped because its character or group couldn't be imported.

memory.queued: Memory summary started; it will show in the chat's memory shortly.
memory.not_needed: Not long enough to need a summary.
memory.unavailable: No model is available for memory, so it wasn't summarized.

dropped.label: Left out: {list}
dropped.system: {count, plural, one {# SillyTavern system message} other {# SillyTavern system messages}}
dropped.empty: {count, plural, one {# empty message} other {# empty messages}}
dropped.malformed: {count, plural, one {# unreadable line} other {# unreadable lines}}
dropped.overLimit: {count, plural, one {# message} other {# messages}} past 20,000
dropped.swipes: {count, plural, one {# swipe} other {# swipes}} past 20 per message
dropped.swipesOverRows: {count, plural, one {# swipe} other {# swipes}} let go to fit the 20,000 per-chat limit
dropped.variables: {count, plural, one {# variable} other {# variables}} too long or past the limits
dropped.attachments: {count, plural, one {# picture or file} other {# pictures or files}} that could not come over

run.unknownSpeaker: {count, plural, one {# message} other {# messages}} with an unknown speaker came in as narration.

warnings.world_unreadable: Couldn't read the lorebook file, imported without it: {name}
warnings.extras_failed: Couldn't attach the extra lorebooks and scripts: {message}
warnings.avatar_failed: Couldn't bring over the persona's picture: {message}
warnings.group_turns_failed: Couldn't bring over the group's turn order and talkativeness: {message}

notices.chat_world_attached: The lorebook bound to this chat, {name}, is now part of the plot's lorebook, so it also applies to the plot's other chats.
notices.note_moved: The author's note came over with its frequency and role, but SillyTavern placed it before or after the story string, which has no match here, so it goes at the start of the chat history.
notices.chat_branch_merged: Added to the {name} chat as a branch (a SillyTavern branch or checkpoint). Swipe to it on the message where the two part.

run.modelUnavailable: Chats need a model to go on. Connect ChatGPT in <link>Settings</link>, then retry — the characters are already in.

rights.creator: Creator
rights.moduleLike: This looks like a RisuAI module file. To add it to the work as a module, use “Import module” under Custom UI instead.

tenseHints.unset: Leaves the tense to the model.
tenseHints.past: Tells what happened as something already done.
tenseHints.present: Tells what happens as it happens.

replyLengthHints.short: One or two paragraphs, and a lower token cap to hold it there.
replyLengthHints.medium: Two or three paragraphs, at an easy reading pace.
replyLengthHints.long: Three to five paragraphs, with a higher token cap to match.
replyLengthHints.auto: Leaves the length to the scene.

deliveryHints.dialogue: Leans a little more on what is said.
deliveryHints.action: Leans a little more on what is done.

pacingHints.fast: Pushes the scene on without lingering.
pacingHints.natural: Moves at whatever pace the scene asks for.
pacingHints.slow: Stays with a scene and lets it take its time.

difficultyHints.easy: The cast mostly goes along with what you lead with.
difficultyHints.normal: The cast reacts as the scene warrants.
difficultyHints.hard: The cast does not cooperate easily, and tension stays in the room.
difficultyHints.nightmare: The cast has a will of its own and turns it against you.

style.moodsHint: Up to {max} of them. Picking another one releases the one you picked first.

storytellingHints.highSociety: Polished wit and feeling held in reserve.
storytellingHints.noir: Dry, sharp sentences with a cold suspense under them.
storytellingHints.afterDark: Sensual prose that makes no apology for wanting.
storytellingHints.blockbuster: Explosive and cinematic, one scene driving into the next.
storytellingHints.arcane: Description with wonder and mystery running through it.
storytellingHints.manga: Fast tempo and outsized personality, drawn in prose.
storytellingHints.dread: Ordinary days with something wrong seeping into them.

style.statusWindowHint: Every reply ends with a card of where, when and how everyone is.
style.statusWindowIntroHint: Write a status code block inside an opening and the first scene has one too.

choicesHints.keywords: Two or three short keyword choices at the end of a reply.
choicesHints.sentences: Two or three full-sentence choices at the end of a reply.

chat.directionHint: Wraps action and scene description in *stage direction* marks.
chat.regenerateRoundHint: Redoes this round's replies from the start, with its speakers picked again.
chat.editHint: Edits it in place. The conversation after it stays as it is.
chat.subModelHint: Used by scripts’ auxiliary model calls and background work such as summaries and reply suggestions. By default it is the default sub model in Settings › Models, or the main model when that is empty.

readerPresets.label: My presets
readerPresets.hint: The chosen preset replaces the default prompt (OAI2). Like the default, a preset with a template doesn't read the card's system prompt, as in RisuAI.
readerPresets.empty: This chat uses the default prompt (OAI2). Make a preset to use instead, or import one from RisuAI or SillyTavern; it's saved for your other chats too.
readerPresets.importHint: Imports a RisuAI or SillyTavern preset file (.json, .risup, .risupreset). A RisuAI preset brings its prompt template whole, or without one its main prompt, jailbreak and global note, along with its toggles, module integration and default variables. A SillyTavern preset's Main Prompt and Auxiliary Prompt become the main prompt, and its Post-History Instructions the global note.
readerPresets.name: Name
readerPresets.templateHint: This template is the prompt. Its items' types and order stay as they are; you can edit their text and inner formats. A negative position in a chat range counts from the end.
readerPresets.innerFormatHint: The inner format: the content goes where '{{slot}}' stands. Left empty, the content is sent as is.
readerPresets.legacyHint: A RisuAI preset without a template: the three texts below are sent in the preset's order.
readerPresets.mainHint: A card with a system prompt sends that instead, with this text where it says '{{original}}'.
readerPresets.jailbreakHint: In RisuAI's default order, it goes right after the chat history. As in RisuAI, it is sent only while the chat's jailbreak toggle is on.
readerPresets.globalNoteHint: A card with post-history instructions sends those instead, with this text where they say '{{original}}'.
readerPresets.togglesHint: RisuAI's preset toggles: one per line as key=name (a choice is key=name=select=a,b). They come first among the chat's toggles, and your instructions read them with '{{#when::toggle::key}}'.
readerPresets.moduleIntegrationHint: Module namespaces separated by commas (e.g. module1,module2). A chat using this preset turns on your modules with those namespaces.
readerPresets.defaultVariablesHint: RisuAI's preset default variables. One name=value per line: in a chat using this preset, a variable nothing has set yet reads as that value. The work's own defaults come first.
readerPresets.imported: Imported from a {source} preset. Save to keep it.
readerPresets.importedNothing: This {source} preset has no prompts, template, toggles, module integration or default variables to import.
readerPresets.tookTemplate: Prompt template → Prompt template ({count, plural, one {# item} other {# items}})
readerPresets.tookPromptSettings: Prompt settings → this preset's prompt settings (not editable here)
readerPresets.tookRegex: {count, plural, one {# preset regex script} other {# preset regex scripts}} → run on what is sent, ahead of the card's (not editable here)
readerPresets.ignoredPrompts: {count, plural, one {# other prompt isn't} other {# other prompts aren't}} sent: {names}
readerPresets.ignoredSettings: Model, sampling and other settings were not imported either.
readerPresets.importUnsupported: That isn't a RisuAI or SillyTavern preset file.

chat.authorNoteHint: An instruction for this chat only. It goes in right before the recent messages.
chat.authorNotePlaceholder: e.g. It's a rainy night from here on. Keep replies short.
chat.attachedNotesHint: Notes from the Notes page, injected after the author's note in order.
chat.attachedNotesEmpty: No saved notes yet. Create one on the Notes page first.
chat.memoryHint: Older parts of a long chat are remembered as a set of summaries. Each reply sends the important ones first, then recent, similar and random ones, up to the memory share.
chat.memoryModelDownloading: The memory model is still downloading. Until it is here, memory sends recent and random summaries instead of similar ones, and no facts are noted.
chat.memoryModelMissing: The memory model could not be downloaded; the app tries again the next time it starts. Until then, memory sends recent and random summaries instead of similar ones, and no facts are noted.
chat.memoryDeleteConfirm: Delete this summary? The messages it covered are summarized again next time.
chat.memoryFactsHint: When a summary is written, the lasting facts in its messages (names, promises, preferences, relationships, important objects) are noted separately, and facts the story has since changed or ended are corrected. Each reply sends the facts closest to the latest turns as [기억], leaving out what the summaries it sends already say.
chat.memoryFactsEmpty: No facts noted on this branch yet.
chat.memoryEndedHint: Changed or ended later in the story, so they are no longer sent. Restore one if it was changed by mistake.

memorySetting.summarizationPromptHint: Leave empty for RisuAI's default. Written in ChatML, the messages go where '{{slot}}' is.

chat.memorySettingsHint: For this chat only. When the chat no longer fits the context budget, the oldest messages are summarized first.
chat.narratorVoicePlaceholder: e.g. Dry, in short clipped sentences.
chat.narratorPovThirdLimited: Third person limited — the scene and the characters only, never the user's inner thoughts
chat.narratorHint: The narrator for this chat only. Leave it empty to follow the one set on the plot.
chat.statusWindowHint: Turn this off and replies in this chat stop ending with a status block. The ones already written stay.
chat.choicesHint: Turn this off and replies in this chat stop offering choices, and no buttons are drawn.
chat.emotionProcessorHint: How each reply picks its expression picture. The auxiliary model reads the reply and names a picture; embedding similarity finds the name closest to the reply with the server's embedding model, without calling the auxiliary model.
chat.lockedWhileGenerating: Can't be changed while a reply is generating.
chat.sendMaybeDelivered: This message may already have been sent. Reload to check before sending it again.
chat.customUiHint: Turn this off to read messages exactly as written, without the plot's panels and buttons.
chat.componentNavigated: The component tried to navigate its frame elsewhere, so it was stopped.
chat.componentTimeout: The component did not respond in time, so loading it was stopped.
chat.componentTurnsHint: Lets this plot's components send messages on your behalf in this chat. Turn it off any time; you will be asked again the next time one tries.
chat.componentTurnConsent: A component of {name} wants to send a message on your behalf. If you allow it, its components may send another one each time a reply finishes in this chat. Allow it? You can take it back from the notes panel at any time.
chat.togglesHint: Settings your preset, the work and the modules you turned on declare. As in RisuAI, their values (toggle_…) are shared by your chats with every work. A value this work kept of its own before they were shared stays on it alone until you change it here.
chat.jailbreakToggleHint: While on, the preset's jailbreak items are sent too. Off to start with, as in RisuAI, and kept like a toggle: shared by your chats with every work.

chat.scriptCommandHelp:
Slash commands (RisuAI). Chain commands with |: each command's result goes into the next as '{{pipe}}', and a command given no text uses the result before it.
/input [text] — asks for a line, and the answer is the result
/echo [text], /popup [text] — shows the text; the result stays as it was
/pass [text] — the text is the result
/buttons labels=["a","b"] — offers the labels; the number of the one chosen, from 0, is the result
/send [text] — adds it to the chat as your message
/sendas [text] — adds it to the chat as the character's message
/comment [text] — adds a comment to the last message
/cut [from-to] — keeps only the messages in that range; /cut [n] keeps only message n
/del [n] — keeps only the last n messages
/len [JSON list] — the number of items is the result
/setvar key=[name] [value], /addvar key=[name] [number], /getvar key=[name] — chat variables
/test_lorebook — shows the lore that is active now
/trigger [name] — runs the story's button trigger of that name
/speak — does nothing here
/? — this list
Messages are numbered from 0 after the opening. A line with a command not on this list is sent as an ordinary message.

devices.description: Opens this computer's shizue in your phone's browser. The button opens a tunnel and shows a QR code; scan it with your phone's camera to open the address and connect to this computer's shizue, which uses the ChatGPT this computer connected. The code works once, for 5 minutes.

devices.pairMissing: There's no pairing code here. Scan the QR code in your computer's settings again.
devices.viaTailscale: Opens through Tailscale. Only devices signed in to the same Tailscale account can reach it, and the phone needs the Tailscale app. The address stays the same each time.
devices.viaCloudflare: Opens through a Cloudflare Quick Tunnel. The phone needs no app, but the address is open on the internet and changes every time; a device that isn't paired sees nothing. With Tailscale installed it opens at a fixed address only your devices reach.
devices.noTool: There is nothing to open a tunnel with. Install Tailscale (recommended, tailscale.com) or cloudflared, then reload this page.
devices.openCloudflare: Open through a Cloudflare Quick Tunnel:
devices.viaDownload: This computer has neither Tailscale nor cloudflared. Opening downloads cloudflared {version} (about {size} MB) as Cloudflare publishes it on GitHub into shizue's folder, checks it against the SHA-256 shizue carries, and opens a Cloudflare Quick Tunnel. The phone needs no app, but the address is open on the internet and changes every time; a device that isn't paired sees nothing. With Tailscale installed it opens at a fixed address only your devices reach.
devices.downloadFailed: cloudflared did not download. Check the network and open it again.

backup.title: Backup and restore
backup.description: Downloads everything in the app folder as one file — works and chats, personas, presets, modules and pictures. It can be made while shizue runs.
backup.secretNote: The backup leaves out this install’s secret, which locks your API keys and ChatGPT connection. Restored on this computer they open as before; restored on another computer, enter the API keys and connect ChatGPT again.
backup.restoreDescription: Checks the backup file, unpacks it into a new folder beside the current one, and switches to it the next time shizue starts. The current folder is kept beside it, not deleted.
backup.pending: The backup made {date} is waiting to be restored. Quit shizue and start it again to switch — anything changed before then stays only in the current folder.
backup.restored: Restored from the backup made {date}. The folder from before is kept at {path}; delete it once you no longer need it.
backup.localOnly: A restore can only be done on the computer shizue runs on.
